amd-cpu.description: AMD arm C: the CPU block matcher's motion and depth proxy, handed to the evaluator in memory; the runtime's temporal model runs under the recording-lease lifecycle. Guides dumped for arm Z's depth and the round-trip proof. Requires DLSS5_AMD_RUNTIME_DIR in the environment (or --amd-runtime-dir).

amd-cpu-nzmt.description: AMD arm C': arm C with the zero-motion test on - a frame byte-identical to its predecessor renders with a zero field, the host-side mirror of NvofResolveShader.h's test. Everything else is bit-for-bit arm C, so still-hold deltas are attributable to held-frame noise alone. It dumps to cpu-nzmt/ rather than cpu/ because its field is not arm C's (the held frames are zeroed), and arm C's dump is what arm Z and the round-trip proof read - two arms writing one directory would let whichever ran last decide the other's input.

amd-zmv.description: AMD arm Z: the zero motion field (guidefiles.py zero) with arm C's dumped depth replayed, so the only difference from arm C is the motion field. Run amd-cpu first; both arms run the temporal model under the same lease lifecycle.

amd-cpu-replay.description: AMD round-trip proof: arm C's dump fed back through the file path. The render must be byte-identical to amd-cpu's (the dump is grid-sized, the file path's area average copies at equal size, and both arms compact the three-channel PFM the same way). Only meaningful on the build with the motion stride fix in AmdLmxxfEvaluator::UploadGuides.

amd-ffx.description: AMD arm F: FidelityFX Optical Flow's motion field with arm C's dumped depth replayed, so the motion field is the only difference from arm Z - AMD's own GPU estimator against the zero field this backend ships. Run amd-cpu first; arm F reads its depth dump, and it has no depth of its own. Needs a build configured with -DFFX_SDK_ROOT and an AMD adapter; the flow reads its field back to memory, so it is an offline arm by construction and never runs on playback.
